_comment: The dark-launch fixture: one description of a fleet, read by the hub's
integration test and by the browser's, so the two can be shown to agree
before the browser's copy of the rules is deleted.
Every timestamp is an OFFSET IN SECONDS from a reference `now` each side
picks for itself, so the fixture does not rot and neither side has to be
run at a particular time of day.
The verdicts below are not a reading of the rules written by hand. They
were produced by RUNNING the pre-change derivation over this fleet --
fleetConditions and fullestFilesystem as of 9213f80, before any of it was
deleted -- and both halves of the gate now assert that answer. That is
what makes 'the hub agrees with the browser' a claim rather than a hope:
the hub half proves the hub produces these verdicts, the browser half
proves the renderer prints them, and this list is what the browser said
when it still decided for itself.
The samples sit on exact step boundaries, and that is load-bearing rather
than tidy. The hub's disk onset is a raw filesystem_samples.ts; the
browser's is a BUCKET EDGE, window.from + index * step. They are the same
instant only when each sample lands on one, so a fixture written off the
grid would produce a disagreement that is an artefact of the fixture and
would get 'fixed' by loosening the assertion.
What is deliberately NOT here, and why:
sporadic  - a rate over missing buckets. The browser counts them over
whatever range the reader picked and the hub over a fixed
three hours, so the two do not agree on a tick boundary and
cannot be made to without one of them lying.
never-seen hosts - the hub refuses to judge them (scanHosts marks them
Unjudged), because a critical event in the gap between
creating a host and installing its agent is false history in
the log alerting reads. The page still says it, synthesised
by the renderer from last_seen === null.
stale subjects - the hub keeps the condition open and marks it; the old
browser dropped the mount after 180 s. That difference is the
point of serving `stale`, not a disagreement to reconcile.

filesystems.label: root
filesystems._comment: 97 GiB used, 3 GiB free: over both halves of the compound rule. Healthy until it crossed at -180 s.

filesystems.label: var
filesystems._comment: Healthy throughout, so the fullest-mount pick has something to beat.

filesystems.label: ark
_comment: 91% of a 6.7 TB array, with 674 GB free. The case the compound
rule exists for: netra used to say '90% full -- 674.4 GB free' in
one breath and expect someone to act on it. Neither side flags it.

hosts._comment: Silent: last heard from an hour ago, well past three scrapes.
Nothing wrong with it. A fleet where every host is broken proves nothing about the healthy path.

expect._comment: The count comes from services_failed; the names and the onset from the unit rows, and five units failing at five times is one condition that began with the first.

expect.subject: root
expect._comment: Walked back to the sample it crossed on, which is the whole payoff: not the moment netra happened to look.
The one condition whose onset needs no derivation: last_seen IS the moment.
